newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fischler says EU dairy quotas, prices need reform.
newsitem.headline: Fischler says EU dairy quotas, prices need reform.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said the EU milk quota system needed to be reformed so that EU producers could compete in expanding world markets for milk and dairy products.
Speaking at a news conference during a German farm fair, he said, "Consumption in the EU will not rise and we need to export more -- but not with the help of massive subsidies."
"We won't be able to operate without quotas, but they should be made more flexible," he said.
The Commission is due to present a discussion paper on dairy reform, the most prominent EU farm topic apart from beef, before an informal farm ministers meeting at the end of May.
The current quota system expires at the end of March 2000.
Fischler said the quota system did not only regulate production but also preserved dairy farming in structually weak regions.
But the practice of leasing or selling unused allocations had distorted the system as it subsidised non-active dairy farmers and penalised others by inflating milk prices.
Fischler did not directly advocate milk price cuts, but said quota cuts alone would not help stabilise prices.
Instead, they would prevent the EU from exporting and pave the way for more imports.
